chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ubaydullah ibn Umar was made to stand, and he had drunk wine, so Umar ordered that he be struck. No one stepped forward to strike him until Ali (peace be upon him) arose with a doubled belt and struck him with it forty times.'

key_terms.النِّسْعَة: A type of belt or strap

ai.seo_question: How did Ali (peace be upon him) administer the hadd penalty for drinking wine?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practical application of the hadd penalty for wine consumption during the early Caliphate, specifically illustrating the method of flogging with a 'nis'a' (a doubled leather belt) as practiced by Ali ibn Abi Talib. It underscores the communal responsibility in administering justice, as Ali stepped in only after no one else volunteered, reflecting the dignity and precision expected in executing divine punishments. This incident is often cited by Shia scholars to validate the specific physical manner of punishment prescribed in the Sunnah.
